Author: namibj
Content:
I have a pretty concrete concept/approach proposal for a "muxed e-test" that'd work with a slightly fancier multimeter than the COB bond test jig already in use, and would utilize a dense analog switch (transmission gate) based bus to connect a variety (think 200 on a full slot) of DUTs in 4-wire like "kelvin" connectivity to external pins to have separate sense and drive wires for all the contact/via/"pin" zones of the DUTs; to be used with e.g. Xyce predictor based selection of what operating points to measure under DC or near-DC conditions, in order to fine-tune the SPICE model of e.g. an SCL and use the 1000 such dies via their cheap COB bonding and a simple test jig (just needs decent volt/current meters behind for good measurements) to get statistically significant data on mismatch across similar structures right besides one another, across reticles on a wafer, and across wafers of a lot.

I'd think it could be scripted with librelane I just don't have the time to do that myself; in lieau of that it could be scripted with klayout (or magic) as it's essentially just a bus with switches underneath DUTs on one side and a digital decoder logic on the other side that just allows for externally selecting which DUT to mux to the bus. Just a decoder into one-hot select bits across the DUT slots should suffice.

DUTs would be SCL cells of sufficient notability, and a bunch of primitives that are lacking foundry open-source e-test coverage (e.g. there's no data on vias/contacts, there's no coverage for thin oxide native nmos at all, there's no coverage for (admittedly kinda DRC-breaking though IMO that's ERC domain and should be waived for at least test structures if modeling is good enough) short channel native NMOS, a LOT of devices lack mismatch characterization (e.g. shottkey diodes are just a start)).
No dynamic behavior intended.
I would like some latchup-type structures if they can be wired to be provoked into latchup with that analog mux, to get at least a hint of e-test coverage for such behavior as it ma not be catastrophic if the chip is prevented from melting itself via teh ensuing power dissipation.
